mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.5% (current level) compresses discount rates for equity valuations, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate prolonged accommodative policy.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS remains below 0.5% (historical data 2005-2024).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in federal funds rate exceeding 0.5 percentage points triggers immediate equity sell-offs due to rising discount rates, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS rises by >0.5pp over 3 months (2005-2024).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous non-farm payrolls growth exceeding 0.1% and unemployment rate decline exceeding 0.1 percentage points in one month signal a tightening labor market, boosting consumer spending and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth > 0.1% and UNRATE decline > 0.1pp in 1 month
failure_condition: The joint signal (PAYEMS growth > 0.1% and UNRATE decline > 0.1pp) fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of cases (2005-2024).

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion (GDP growth > 2.5% annualized), a decline in housing starts below 1000 thousand units signals weakening consumer demand, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansion (GDPC1 growth > 2.5% annualized), HOUST decline below 1000 thousand units fails to produce negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production growth above 1.5% annualized signals robust manufacturing output, supporting corporate earnings and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO growth above 1.5% annualized fails to produce positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances (2005-2024).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month Consumer Price Index increase exceeding 0.3 percentage points per month signals accelerating inflation, triggering central bank tightening and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL rises by >0.3pp over 3 months (2005-2024).

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion (GDP growth > 2.5% annualized), an unemployment rate below 5.0% signals a tight labor market that fuels consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansion (GDPC1 growth > 2.5% annualized), UNRATE below 5.0% fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous federal funds rate increase exceeding 0.25 percentage points and CPIAUCSL rise exceeding 0.2 percentage points in one month signal aggressive monetary tightening amid inflation, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rise > 0.25pp and CPIAUCSL rise > 0.2pp in 1 month
failure_condition: The joint signal (FEDFUNDS rise > 0.25pp and CPIAUCSL rise > 0.2pp) fails to produce negative 5-day returns in more than 50% of cases (2005-2024).
